learnerStatement: Simulated learner. This review finds problems; it is not evidence that anyone learned.
learnerBoundary: Everyday numeracy, simple charts, comparing numbers and familiar household objects; no domain-specific theory assumed.

observations.prediction: Selected Same either way and locked the prediction for $100k with one +25% year, one -20% year, and $20k withdrawn at each year end.
observations.exploration: Loss first ended at $55k; switching to gain first ended at $64k. Setting cash flow to zero made both end at $100k. Depositing $20k instead reversed the advantage: gain first $136k, loss first $145k. Selected loss first to inspect that path.
observations.reveal: The reveal corrected the withdrawal prediction to gain first. It explained that multiplication order alone does not change the final balance, but withdrawals remove money from a smaller pot after a loss; deposits reverse the advantage.
observations.visual: Inspected the dark 1257 by 936 inline screenshot with deposits. A solid mint loss first path ended at $145k above a dashed gain first path at $136k. The comparison history preserved all three cash flow conditions below the chart.
observations.isolation: No-history evaluation preview banner present. Visible trust count ignored.
observations.reference: Own CUA tab 543884163 snapshots and inspected inline screenshot; no screenshot file saved.

prediction.reason: The apparent symmetry invites a specific testable commitment.
prediction.evidence: Selected same either way for equal annual withdrawals.

interaction.reason: A single cash flow control exposes the boundary and reverses the result.
interaction.evidence: Withdrawals favored gain first, zero tied, deposits favored loss first.

payoff.reason: The explanation connects each observed condition to money available for recovery.
payoff.evidence: Reveal included $64k, $55k and the deposit reversal to $145k.

clarity.reason: The paths and persistent comparison history make the contrast easy to follow.
clarity.evidence: Selected solid path and dashed alternative had explicit endpoint labels.

transfer.reason: The lesson supplies a usable condition for interpreting return sequences.
transfer.evidence: Cash flows make order matter; withdrawals and deposits can favor opposite sequences.

accessibility.evidence: Keyboard, focus, contrast audit, phone, zoom/reflow and motion unknown.

surprise.reason: The same returns can favor either ordering depending on cash flow.
surprise.evidence: Changing withdrawal to deposit reversed the winner.

visualExplanation.reason: The two paths support comparison across identical start and end times.
visualExplanation.evidence: Solid and dashed lines shared the $100k starting point and labelled endpoints.

playfulness.reason: Sliding through a tie to a reversal makes a compact exploration.
playfulness.evidence: Cash flow zero and positive values changed the relationship immediately.

practicalValue.reason: The mechanism is relevant to saving and withdrawing decisions.
practicalValue.evidence: The reveal distinguishes contribution timing from withdrawal timing.

depth.reason: It reaches beyond one outcome to explain the condition and reversal.
depth.evidence: The zero cash flow equality and opposite deposit result were both explored.

complexity.reason: Percent growth and annual cash flows need careful ordering, while the controls are straightforward.
complexity.conceptualDemand: Moderate: separate return multiplication from intervening additions or withdrawals.
complexity.interfaceBurden: Low: two ordering buttons and one cash flow slider.
complexity.conceptualChallenge: Cash flow changes the amount exposed to the following year's return.
complexity.prerequisiteNovelty: Basic percentages and compounding are required.
complexity.notationRepresentationBurden: Low to moderate: dollar chart and multiplier notation.

whyCool: A tie becomes one winner or the opposite winner simply by changing whether money enters or leaves.
caveat: The toy fixes two annual returns and cash flow timing; it does not model uncertain real returns or costs.
missingEvidence: No fresh return pair was available.
